result.title: Self-Improving Video-to-Action Models
result.comment: 33 pages, 18 figures, 6 tables. Project page: https://wilcoxsonm21.github.io/mirror/
result.summary: Video generative models are an emerging tool for embodied agents: they can serve as scalable visual planners, generating videos that depict how to complete previously unseen tasks. However, executing these plans typically requires a video-to-action or "inverse dynamics" model trained on large, human-collected video-action datasets, severely limiting scalability. We introduce Mirror, a self-supervised approach that learns video-to-action mappings through environment interactions, without prior action data or hand-crafted rewards. Mirror learns by attempting to follow a visual plan by executing its best guess of the underlying actions in the environment. Mirror then trains on the resulting video-action pairs, incrementally self-improving and following the visual planner more closely. Across Atari, OGBench, and DeepMind Control, Mirror outperforms leading learning-from-observation methods with learned video plans, and achieves near-expert performance with oracle plans. On Minecraft BASALT, it outperforms methods with access to expert actions or hand-engineered task knowledge. In Minecraft survival, it is the first method to acquire an iron pickaxe through self-improvement alone, without rewards or expert action labels. In the offline setting, with expert action labels but no environment interaction, it sets a new state of the art in obtaining diamonds. Our results suggest that advances in video models can translate into increasingly capable agents without a corresponding need for hand-crafted rewards or large collections of expert action data.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Mirror：在无动作标签和无奖励的前提下，通过尝试执行视频规划器给出的视觉计划生成 video-action 对，自监督训练 video-to-action 逆动力学模型并迭代自我改进，在 Atari、OGBench、DMC 与 Minecraft 上超过既有模仿学习方法。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「视觉计划→环境执行→回填监督」闭环可能为 LVR 中 latent 状态如何解码为可检验动作、以及无标注轨迹训练与贡献分配提供借鉴线索，可供核查；但论文面向具身控制，未涉及 VLM 内部推理状态本身。
